- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.8) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model forecasts peak too early and then underperforms in subsequent days.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model often forecasts a price that is too far from recent average, especially when sentiment is volatile.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model takes 2–3 days to adjust to sentiment changes, leading to delayed corrections.
- Overweight recent history in short-term forecasts — model overfits to recent price movements, ignoring sentiment-driven structural shifts.
- Underweight sentiment in long-term forecasts — model ignores sentiment trends when projecting 30-day horizons, leading to persistent bias.
